misconceptions.description: Treating the capstone package as a folder of finished files rather than a coherent argument where the iteration log, defense, and presentation tell one consistent story
misconceptions.trigger: package zips six artifacts that contradict each other or never reference one another
misconceptions.feedback: A defensible package is internally consistent: the claims in the presentation match the iteration log, the AI-USE.md, and the quality review. Assembly is not coherence.

misconceptions.description: Letting one capstone component claim something a sibling component contradicts, such as a talk citing a tryout the iteration log never records
misconceptions.trigger: presentation references evidence that does not appear in the iteration log or quality review
misconceptions.feedback: Cross-check claims across components before submitting; a committee will notice when the talk and the log disagree.

misconceptions.description: Submitting the package without a synthesis that names what changed across the module and what the designer would do differently next time
misconceptions.trigger: completion artifact restates each deliverable but never reflects on the arc of decisions
misconceptions.feedback: Add a synthesis that traces how your design judgment changed across the module, not just a list of what you produced.

misconceptions.description: Asking AI to assemble or summarize the whole package and submitting it without verifying that the summary matches each underlying artifact
misconceptions.trigger: AI-written package overview states accomplishments the artifacts do not support
misconceptions.feedback: If AI helps assemble or summarize the package, verify every statement against the real components before you submit and defend it.
